docs/knowledgebase/KB_ExchangeOnline_Man.title: How to Manage Distribution Group Membership | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_ExchangeOnline_Man.summary: Description Instructions for managing distribution group membership in Exchange Online. Details Distribution groups in Exchange Online allow users to communicate with multiple recipients using a single email address. Membership can be managed by users or group owners, depending on permissions. Some groups may require approval to join or leave, and changes may take time to sync. Understanding how to manage group membership helps ensure you receive relevant communications and can collaborate effectively. Information How to Join or Leave a Distribution Group Sign in to Outlook Web App at Outlook Web App. Click 'Settings' > 'View all Outlook settings' > 'Mail' > 'Groups'. Find the distribution group and click 'Join' or 'Leave'. How to Manage Group Membership (Owners) Owners can add or remove members via Outlook Web App or the Microsoft 365 admin center. In Outlook Web App, go to 'Groups', select the group, and click 'Edit group'. In Microsoft 365 admin center, go to 'Groups' > 'Active groups', select the group, and manage membership. Additional Information and Follow-up Some groups may require approval to join or leave. Changes may take a few minutes to sync across services. If you cannot manage your group membership, contact your IT support or group owner. For further assistance, contact your IT support or the group owner. References Microsoft: Manage distribution groups in Outlook Microsoft: Microsoft 365 Groups management

docs/knowledgebase/KB_ExchangeOnline_Man.title: How to Manage Mailbox Size and Clean Up Old Emails | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_ExchangeOnline_Man.summary: Description Instructions for managing mailbox size and cleaning up old emails in Outlook. Details Mailbox size management is essential to avoid reaching storage limits and ensure optimal performance in Outlook and Exchange Online. Regularly cleaning up old emails, archiving important messages, and removing large attachments can help keep your mailbox within quota. Organizations may enforce mailbox quotas based on licensing, and exceeding these quotas can prevent you from sending or receiving new emails. Information How to Check Mailbox Size in Outlook Open Outlook and click 'File'. Select 'Tools' > 'Mailbox Cleanup'. Click 'View Mailbox Size' to see details. How to Clean Up Old Emails Use 'Mailbox Cleanup' to find items older than a certain date. Empty the 'Deleted Items' and 'Junk Email' folders. Archive old emails using Outlook's Archive feature. Delete large attachments or move them to OneDrive/SharePoint. In Outlook Web App (OWA) Sign in to Outlook Web App. Right-click folders and select 'Empty folder' to delete all items. Use search to find and delete old or large emails. Additional Information and Follow-up Mailbox quotas are enforced by Exchange Online; exceeding quota may prevent sending/receiving mail. Archiving helps keep mailbox size within limits and improves performance. Use OneDrive or SharePoint for storing large files instead of email attachments. If you need help managing mailbox size or archiving, contact your IT support or helpdesk. References Microsoft: Manage mailbox size in Outlook Microsoft: Archive older items manually in Outlook

docs/knowledgebase/KB_ExchangeOnline_Quo.title: What to Do If You Reach Your Mailbox Quota or Send Limit | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_ExchangeOnline_Quo.summary: Description Guidance for users who reach their mailbox quota or send limit in Exchange Online. Details Mailbox quotas and send limits are enforced to maintain service reliability and prevent abuse. If you reach these limits, you may be unable to send or receive emails until you reduce mailbox size or wait for limits to reset. Regular mailbox maintenance and awareness of limits can help prevent disruptions. If issues persist, IT support can assist with quota increases or troubleshooting. Information What Happens When You Reach Your Quota or Send Limit You may be unable to send or receive new emails. You may receive a warning message or a non-delivery report (NDR). Your mailbox may stop syncing with Outlook or mobile devices. Steps to Take Delete unnecessary emails, especially those with large attachments. Empty your 'Deleted Items' and 'Junk Email' folders. Archive old emails using Outlook's Archive feature. Use OneDrive or SharePoint for sharing large files. If you need to send to more recipients, split your message into smaller groups. Additional Information and Follow-up Mailbox quotas and send limits are set by your organization and Microsoft 365 licensing. If you continue to have issues, you may need to request a quota increase (see related KB article). If you cannot resolve the issue, contact your IT support or helpdesk for assistance. References Microsoft: Exchange Online mailbox quotas and limits Microsoft: Reduce mailbox size

docs/knowledgebase/KB_ExchangeOnline_Rec.title: How to Recover Deleted Emails and Items | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_ExchangeOnline_Rec.summary: Description Instructions for recovering deleted emails and items in Outlook and OWA. Details Exchange Online retains deleted emails and items for a limited time, allowing users to recover them if deleted accidentally. Items in the 'Deleted Items' folder are typically retained for 30 days, and some organizations enable additional recovery from the server for up to 14 days. Recovery options may vary depending on your organization's retention policies and permissions. Always check both the 'Deleted Items' folder and server recovery options before contacting IT support. Information Recover Deleted Items in Outlook (Windows/Mac) Open Outlook and go to the 'Deleted Items' folder. Locate the email or item you want to recover. Right-click the item and select 'Move' > 'Inbox' or another folder. If the item is not in 'Deleted Items', go to 'Home' > 'Recover Deleted Items from Server'. Select the items to restore and click 'Restore Selected Items'. Recover Deleted Items in Outlook Web App (OWA) Sign in to Outlook Web App at Outlook Web App. Go to the 'Deleted Items' folder. Select the item and click 'Restore'. If not found, click 'Recover items deleted from this folder' at the top. Select items and click 'Restore'. Additional Information and Follow-up Items in 'Deleted Items' are retained for 30 days by default. After 30 days, items may be recoverable from the server for up to 14 days (if enabled by your organization). Permanently deleted items cannot be recovered after retention period expires. If you cannot recover your item, contact your IT support or helpdesk for further assistance. References Microsoft: Recover deleted items in Outlook Microsoft: Recover deleted email messages in Outlook on the web

docs/knowledgebase/KB_ExchangeOnline_Req.title: How to Request a Mailbox Quota Increase | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_ExchangeOnline_Req.summary: Description Instructions for requesting a mailbox quota increase in Exchange Online. Details Mailbox quota increases may be necessary for users with large volumes of email or specific business needs. Requests are subject to organizational policy and Microsoft 365 licensing. Before requesting an increase, clean up your mailbox and archive old items to ensure efficient use of storage. IT support will review your request and advise on next steps. Information How to Request a Mailbox Quota Increase Contact your IT support or helpdesk and provide your mailbox details. Explain why you need a quota increase (e.g., business need, large volume of email). Your IT team will review your request and may adjust your quota based on licensing and policy. What to Expect Quota increases are subject to organizational policy and Microsoft 365 licensing. You may be asked to clean up your mailbox before a quota increase is approved. Changes may take up to 24 hours to apply. Additional Information and Follow-up Standard mailbox quotas are 50 GB (E1/E3) and 100 GB (E5). Archiving and cleaning up your mailbox may resolve quota issues without an increase. If your request is denied or you need further assistance, contact your IT support or helpdesk. References Microsoft: Exchange Online mailbox quotas and limits Microsoft: Reduce mailbox size

docs/knowledgebase/KB_ExchangeOnline_Sen.title: Understanding Exchange Online Send/Receive Limits | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_ExchangeOnline_Sen.summary: Description Overview of send and receive limits in Exchange Online. Details Exchange Online enforces limits on message size, recipient count, and mailbox storage to ensure reliable service and prevent abuse. These limits may differ based on your organization's licensing and policies. Understanding these limits helps prevent issues with sending, receiving, or storing emails. If you regularly reach these limits, consider using alternative file sharing methods or requesting a quota increase from IT support. Information Exchange Online Send/Receive Limits Maximum message size: 150 MB (default is 35 MB for most organizations) Recipient limit per message: 500 recipients Daily send limit: 10,000 recipients per day Mailbox size limit: 50 GB (E1/E3), 100 GB (E5) Attachment size limit: 150 MB (may be lower for some clients) How to Check Your Limits In Outlook Web App, go to 'Settings' > 'View all Outlook settings' > 'Mail' > 'Message handling'. Ask your IT support for your organization's specific limits. Additional Information and Follow-up Limits may vary based on your organization's policies and licensing. If you exceed a limit, you may receive a non-delivery report (NDR) or error message. Large attachments may be blocked; use OneDrive or SharePoint for sharing large files. If you need higher limits or encounter issues, contact your IT support or helpdesk. References Microsoft: Exchange Online limits Microsoft: Message size and recipient limits

docs/knowledgebase/KB_ExchangeOnline_Upd.title: How to Update Your Contact Information in Exchange Online | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_ExchangeOnline_Upd.summary: Description Instructions for updating your contact information in Exchange Online. Details Updating your contact information ensures colleagues and automated systems have accurate details for communication and collaboration. You may need to update your display name, phone number, office location, or job title if you change roles or locations. Some fields may be restricted by your organization and require IT assistance. Always verify changes after updating, as it may take time for updates to sync across Microsoft 365 services. Information Update Contact Information in Outlook (Windows/Mac) Open Outlook and go to File > Account Settings > Account Settings. Select your account and click 'Change'. Update your contact details (name, email, phone, etc.) as needed. Click 'Next' and then 'Finish'. Restart Outlook to apply changes. Update Contact Information in Outlook Web App (OWA) Sign in to Outlook Web App at Outlook Web App. Click your profile picture in the top right and select 'View account'. Under 'Personal info', click 'Edit' next to the field you want to update. Make changes and click 'Save'. Information That Can Be Updated Display Name Phone Number Office Location Job Title Email Address (if permitted) Additional Information and Follow-up Some fields may be managed by your organization and require IT assistance to update. Changes may take up to 24 hours to sync across Microsoft 365 services. If you cannot update your information, contact your IT support or helpdesk. For further assistance, contact the Identity and Access Management Team or your local IT support. References Microsoft: Change your contact information in Outlook Microsoft: Update your profile in Office 365

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Approve-Signin.title: How to Approve Sign-ins Using Microsoft Authenticator Push Notifications | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Approve-Signin.summary: Description Instructions for approving sign-ins using push notifications in the Microsoft Authenticator App. Details To approve sign-ins using Microsoft Authenticator push notifications: When prompted during sign-in, a notification will appear on your mobile device. Open the Microsoft Authenticator App. Tap "Approve" to confirm the sign-in. If you did not initiate the sign-in, tap "Deny". Tips: Enable notifications for the app on your device. Always deny requests you did not initiate. Issue Resolution: If notifications are not received, check device notification settings and internet connectivity. If unable to approve, restart the app and device, and ensure the app is updated. For persistent issues, sign in using an alternate method and contact IT support. References: Approve sign-ins with Authenticator Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support if you do not receive notifications or have trouble approving sign-ins.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Authenticator-.title: How to Recover Access if You Lose Your Authenticator Device | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Authenticator-.summary: Description Steps to recover access if your Microsoft Authenticator device is lost or unavailable. Details Steps to recover access if your Microsoft Authenticator device is lost or unavailable: Try to sign in using an alternate registered method (SMS, FIDO2 key). If no backup method is available, contact IT support for identity verification. IT may issue a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) or reset your authentication methods. Register your new device with the Authenticator App. Tips: Always register multiple authentication methods. Keep backup codes or alternate contact info. Issue Resolution: If unable to recover access, escalate to IT and request a TAP or manual reset. If you regain access, immediately add backup authentication methods. For persistent issues, document your recovery steps for future reference. References: Recover Authenticator access Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support for urgent recovery or device replacement.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Enable-Passwor.title: How to Enable Passwordless Sign-In | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Enable-Passwor.summary: Description Instructions for enabling passwordless sign-in in your account. Details To enable passwordless sign-in for your account: Go to My Sign-Ins Security Info. Sign in with your Microsoft 365 or Entra ID account. Select "Add method" and choose your preferred passwordless option: Microsoft Authenticator App FIDO2 Security Key Temporary Access Pass (if available) Follow the on-screen instructions to complete setup. Test your passwordless sign-in by logging out and signing in again. Tips: Register more than one passwordless method for backup. Keep your devices and keys secure. Issue Resolution: If setup fails, check for browser compatibility and update your browser. If you do not see passwordless options, contact IT to confirm eligibility. For FIDO2 keys, ensure the key is supported and firmware is up to date. For Authenticator App, verify notifications are enabled and app is updated. References: Enable passwordless sign-in Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support if you encounter issues during setup.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Get-Help-with-.title: How to Get Help or Escalate MFA Issues | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Get-Help-with-.summary: Description How to get help or escalate issues related to multi-factor authentication. Details How to get help or escalate issues related to multi-factor authentication (MFA): Review related KB articles for troubleshooting steps. If you cannot resolve the issue, contact your IT support or help desk. Provide details about your issue (error messages, device type, authentication method). For urgent or unresolved issues, request escalation to the IAM team. Tips: Keep your contact information up to date. Register multiple authentication methods for backup. Issue Resolution: If IT support cannot resolve your issue, request escalation and document all troubleshooting steps taken. For persistent lockout or technical errors, request a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) or manual reset. If you regain access, immediately add backup authentication methods. References: Microsoft: Get help with MFA Additional Information and Follow-up For persistent issues, escalate to IAM team or follow your organization's support process.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Lost-Access-to.title: What to Do If You Lose Access to All MFA Methods | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Lost-Access-to.summary: Description Guidance for users who have lost access to all registered MFA methods. Details If you lose access to all registered MFA methods (Authenticator app, FIDO2 key, phone number): Try to sign in and select "I can't use any of my authentication methods" if available. Contact your IT support or help desk for identity verification and account recovery. Be prepared to provide proof of identity (employee ID, alternate contact, etc.). IT may issue a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) or reset your MFA settings. Tips: Register multiple authentication methods to avoid lockout. Keep your contact information up to date. Issue Resolution: If you cannot access any method, escalate to IT immediately and request a TAP or manual reset. If you regain access to one method, use it to add backup methods in your security info. For urgent cases, request escalation to the IAM team and document your recovery steps for future reference. References: Microsoft: Recover your account Additional Information and Follow-up For urgent issues, escalate to IAM team or follow your organization's recovery process.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Manage-Account.title: How to Add or Remove Accounts in Microsoft Authenticator | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Manage-Account.summary: Description Instructions for adding or removing accounts in the Microsoft Authenticator App. Details To add or remove accounts in the Microsoft Authenticator App: Add an Account: Open the Microsoft Authenticator App on your mobile device. Tap the "+" icon to add a new account. Choose the account type (Work, School, Personal). Scan the QR code or enter the setup code provided by your organization. Follow prompts to complete setup. Remove an Account: Open the Authenticator App. Tap the account you want to remove. Tap the three dots (menu) and select "Remove account". Confirm removal. Tips: Always keep backup methods registered. Remove old accounts you no longer use. Issue Resolution: If unable to add an account, check for app updates and ensure you are scanning the correct QR code. If removal fails, restart the app and try again. If the issue persists, reinstall the app. For work/school accounts, ensure your device is compliant with company policies. References: Microsoft Authenticator setup Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support if you have trouble adding or removing accounts.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Manage-Authent.title: How to Manage Your Authentication Methods in My Sign-Ins Portal | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Manage-Authent.summary: Description Instructions for managing your authentication methods in the My Sign-Ins portal. Details To manage your authentication methods in the My Sign-Ins portal: Go to My Sign-Ins Security Info. Sign in with your Microsoft 365 or Entra ID account. View your registered methods (Authenticator App, FIDO2 key, phone, etc.). Add, remove, or change authentication methods as needed. Follow prompts to verify changes. Tips: Keep multiple methods registered for backup. Remove outdated or unused methods. Issue Resolution: If unable to add or remove a method, check for browser compatibility and update your browser. If changes do not save, clear browser cache and cookies, then retry. For persistent issues, contact IT support for manual updates. References: Manage authentication methods Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support for help managing your authentication methods.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Manage-FIDO2-K.title: How to Remove or Replace a FIDO2 Security Key | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Manage-FIDO2-K.summary: Description Instructions for removing or replacing a FIDO2 security key. Details To remove or replace a FIDO2 security key (including YubiKey): Remove a Key: Go to My Sign-Ins Security Info. Sign in and locate your registered FIDO2 keys (YubiKey or other brands) under "Security keys". Click "Remove" next to the key you want to delete. Add a New Key: Select "Add method" > "Security key". Choose "USB device" or "NFC device" depending on your key model (YubiKey or other). Insert or tap your key when prompted. Set a PIN for your key if required. Complete registration and test sign-in. Tips: Remove lost or unused keys promptly. Register more than one key (YubiKey or other) for backup and redundancy. Store backup keys securely. Use the official YubiKey Manager for advanced YubiKey features. Issue Resolution: If unable to remove a key, refresh the page and try again. If the issue persists, clear browser cache or use a different browser. If new key registration fails, check for firmware updates and use a supported browser. For YubiKey-specific issues, consult Yubico support or use YubiKey Manager for troubleshooting. References: Manage FIDO2 keys YubiKey setup for Microsoft accounts Microsoft: Set up a security key Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support if you have trouble removing or replacing a key.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Overview-Passw.title: Overview of Passwordless Authentication Options | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Overview-Passw.summary: Description Overview of available passwordless authentication options for Microsoft 365 and Entra ID. Details Passwordless authentication options available for Microsoft 365 and Entra ID include: Microsoft Authenticator App: Approve sign-ins with push notifications or use time-based codes. FIDO2 Security Keys: Physical keys that support passwordless sign-in. Temporary Access Pass (TAP): Time-limited pass for onboarding or recovery. SMS Codes: Receive one-time codes via text message. Benefits: Enhanced security Reduced password fatigue Improved user experience References: Microsoft: Passwordless Authentication Troubleshooting Passwordless Authentication Issues Common issues and solutions for passwordless sign-in: Issue: Unable to register a passwordless method Ensure your account is eligible for passwordless options (check with IT if unsure). Use a supported device and browser (Edge, Chrome, Firefox). Clear browser cache and cookies before retrying. Disable browser extensions that may block authentication popups. Contact IT if options are missing or you see error messages. Issue: Sign-in fails with passwordless method Check internet connectivity (Wi-Fi or cellular data must be active). Make sure your device or key is registered and active in your security info. Try an alternate method if available (Authenticator App, FIDO2 key, SMS). Restart your device and browser. If using a FIDO2 key, ensure it is inserted/tapped correctly and PIN is entered. Issue: Authenticator App or FIDO2 key not working Update the app or key firmware to the latest version. Remove and re-add the method in your security info. Confirm your device's date and time settings are set to automatic. References: Troubleshoot passwordless sign-in Additional Information and Follow-up For more details, see related KB articles on setup and troubleshooting. If you continue to experience issues, contact your IT support or refer to related KB articles for setup and troubleshooting.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Register-FIDO2.title: How to Register a FIDO2 Security Key for Passwordless Sign-In | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Register-FIDO2.summary: Description Instructions for registering a FIDO2 security key for passwordless authentication. Details To register a FIDO2 security key for passwordless sign-in: Go to My Sign-Ins Security Info. Sign in and select "Add method" > "Security key". Choose USB or NFC key type and follow prompts. Insert or tap your FIDO2 key when prompted. Set a PIN for your key if required. Complete registration and test sign-in. Tips: Use a supported FIDO2 key (see Microsoft documentation). Register more than one key for backup. Issue Resolution: If your key is not recognized, try a different USB port or NFC reader and check for firmware updates. If PIN is not accepted, reset your key or contact IT. If unable to register, use a supported browser and check for OS/browser updates. References: Register a FIDO2 security key Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support if you encounter issues registering your key.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Register-SMS.h.title: How to Register Your Mobile Number for SMS MFA | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Register-SMS.h.summary: Description Instructions for registering your mobile number for SMS-based multi-factor authentication. Details To register your mobile number for SMS-based MFA: Go to My Sign-Ins Security Info. Sign in and select "Add method" > "Phone". Enter your mobile number and select "Text me a code". Enter the code received via SMS to verify your number. Your phone will be registered for SMS MFA. Tips: Use a mobile number you always have access to. Update your number if it changes. Issue Resolution: If you do not receive the SMS code, check your phone signal and verify your number is correct. If code is delayed or expired, request a new code and restart your device. If unable to register, contact IT for assistance. References: Register phone for MFA Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support if you have trouble registering your number.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Reset-MFA-Sett.title: How to Reset Your MFA Settings | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Reset-MFA-Sett.summary: Description Instructions for resetting your multi-factor authentication settings. Details To reset your multi-factor authentication (MFA) settings: Go to My Sign-Ins Security Info. Sign in and locate your registered authentication methods. Remove outdated or unused methods. Add new methods as needed (Authenticator App, FIDO2 key, phone). Save changes and test sign-in. Tips: Register multiple methods for backup. Contact IT support if you cannot access your account. Issue Resolution: If unable to remove or add methods, clear browser cache and cookies, then retry. If changes do not save, try a different browser or device. For persistent issues, contact IT support for manual reset. References: Reset MFA settings Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support for help resetting your MFA settings.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Setup-Microsof.title: How to Set Up Microsoft Authenticator App for MFA | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Setup-Microsof.summary: Description Step-by-step instructions for setting up the Microsoft Authenticator App for multi-factor authentication (MFA). Details To set up the Microsoft Authenticator App for MFA: Download and install the Microsoft Authenticator App from the App Store or Google Play. Open the app and tap "+" to add an account. On your computer, go to My Sign-Ins Security Info. Sign in and select "Add method" > "Authenticator App". Scan the QR code displayed on your computer with the app. Approve the test notification to complete setup. Tips: Enable app lock for added security. Register backup authentication methods. Issue Resolution: If you do not receive notifications, check device notification settings and internet connectivity. If unable to scan QR code, ensure your camera is working and the code is not expired. If setup fails, update the app and try again or restart your device. References: Set up Microsoft Authenticator Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support if you have trouble setting up the app.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Sign-in-with-S.title: How to Sign In Using SMS Codes | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Sign-in-with-S.summary: Description Steps to sign in using SMS codes for MFA. Details To sign in using SMS codes for MFA: Go to the sign-in page for Microsoft 365 or Entra ID. Enter your username and password. When prompted, select "Text me a code". Enter the code received via SMS. Complete sign-in. Tips: Ensure your mobile number is registered and up to date. If you do not receive a code, check your phone signal or contact IT. Issue Resolution: If SMS code is not received, verify your number and check for carrier issues. If code is delayed or expired, request a new code and restart your device. For persistent issues, contact IT support for manual verification. References: Sign in with SMS Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support if you have trouble receiving or entering SMS codes.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Sign-in-with-T.title: How to Sign In with Temporary Access Pass (TAP) | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Sign-in-with-T.summary: Description Steps to sign in using TAP for first-time setup or lost device scenarios. Details To sign in using Temporary Access Pass (TAP): Obtain a TAP from your IT administrator. Go to the sign-in page for Microsoft 365 or Entra ID. Enter your username and select "Sign in with Temporary Access Pass". Enter the TAP code provided. Register new authentication methods if prompted. Complete sign-in and setup. Tips: TAP is time-limited; use it before it expires. Register backup methods during TAP sign-in. Issue Resolution: If TAP does not work, check for typos and ensure it has not expired. If unable to register new methods, try a different browser or device. If you do not receive a TAP, contact IT and confirm your identity. References: Sign in with TAP Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support if you need a TAP or have trouble signing in.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Switch-to-Pass.title: How to Switch from Password-Based to Passwordless Sign-In | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Switch-to-Pass.summary: Description Steps to switch from password-based to passwordless sign-in. Details To switch from password-based to passwordless sign-in: Go to My Sign-Ins Security Info. Sign in and select "Add method". Choose a passwordless option (Authenticator App, FIDO2 key, TAP). Follow prompts to complete setup. Remove password-based methods if desired. Test your passwordless sign-in. Tips: Register multiple passwordless methods for backup. Contact IT for help with migration. Issue Resolution: If passwordless options are not available, contact IT to confirm eligibility and policy settings. If setup fails, update your browser and clear cache/cookies. For FIDO2 keys, check for firmware updates and use a supported browser. For Authenticator App, ensure notifications are enabled and app is updated. References: Switch to passwordless Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support for help switching authentication methods.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Troubleshoot-A.title: Troubleshooting Microsoft Authenticator App Issues | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Troubleshoot-A.summary: Description Common issues and solutions for the Microsoft Authenticator App. Details Common issues and solutions for the Microsoft Authenticator App: Issue: App not receiving notifications Ensure push notifications are enabled for the app in your device settings (iOS: Settings > Notifications > Authenticator; Android: Settings > Apps > Authenticator > Notifications). Check internet connectivity (Wi-Fi or cellular data must be active). Restart your device to refresh app services. Make sure battery saver or "Do Not Disturb" mode is not blocking notifications. Confirm the app is running in the background and not force-closed. Issue: Unable to add account Make sure you scan the correct QR code from your organization's security portal. Update the app to the latest version via the App Store or Google Play. Try removing and re-adding the account in both the app and your security portal. Clear the app cache (Android: Settings > Apps > Authenticator > Storage > Clear Cache). If using work/school accounts, ensure your device is registered and compliant with company policies. Issue: App not generating codes or codes not accepted Check your device's date and time settings; set to automatic to avoid time drift. Remove and re-add the account to resync codes. Update the app to the latest version. References: Troubleshoot Authenticator App Microsoft Authenticator FAQ Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support for persistent issues, device recovery, or if you cannot access your accounts.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Troubleshoot-F.title: Troubleshooting FIDO2 Security Key Issues | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Troubleshoot-F.summary: Description Common issues and solutions for FIDO2 security key problems. Details Common FIDO2 security key issues and solutions: Issue: Key not recognized Try a different USB port or NFC reader. Ensure your key is supported and registered. Check for firmware updates using the manufacturer's tool (e.g., YubiKey Manager). Issue: PIN not accepted Reset your key if possible using the manufacturer's instructions. Contact IT for assistance if reset fails. Issue: Unable to register key Use a supported browser (Edge, Chrome, Firefox). Check for OS or browser updates. Disable browser extensions that may block authentication popups. References: Troubleshoot FIDO2 keys Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support for persistent issues or key replacement.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Troubleshoot-P.title: Troubleshooting Passwordless Sign-In Issues | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Troubleshoot-P.summary: Description Common issues and solutions for passwordless sign-in problems. Details Common issues and solutions for passwordless sign-in: Issue: Unable to register a passwordless method Ensure your account is eligible for passwordless options (check with IT if unsure). Use a supported device and browser (Edge, Chrome, Firefox). Clear browser cache and cookies before retrying. Disable browser extensions that may block authentication popups. Contact IT if options are missing or you see error messages. Issue: Sign-in fails with passwordless method Check internet connectivity (Wi-Fi or cellular data must be active). Make sure your device or key is registered and active in your security info. Try an alternate method if available (Authenticator App, FIDO2 key, SMS). Restart your device and browser. If using a FIDO2 key, ensure it is inserted/tapped correctly and PIN is entered. Issue: Authenticator App or FIDO2 key not working Update the app or key firmware to the latest version. Remove and re-add the method in your security info. Confirm your device's date and time settings are set to automatic. References: Troubleshoot passwordless sign-in Additional Information and Follow-up If you continue to experience issues, contact your IT support or refer to related KB articles for setup and troubleshooting.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Troubleshoot-S.title: Troubleshooting SMS Code Delivery Issues | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Troubleshoot-S.summary: Description Common issues and solutions for SMS code delivery problems. Details Common issues and solutions for SMS code delivery problems: Issue: Not receiving SMS codes Check your phone signal and carrier. Ensure your mobile number is registered and up to date. Restart your device. Contact IT support for manual verification if the issue persists. Issue: SMS code delayed or expired Wait a few minutes and request a new code. docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Update-Phone-N.summary: Description Instructions for updating or changing your registered phone number for MFA. Details To update or change your registered phone number for MFA: Go to My Sign-Ins Security Info. Sign in and locate your registered phone number. Click "Change" or "Remove" next to your number. Enter your new mobile number and verify with a code. Save changes and test sign-in. Tips: Keep your phone number up to date to avoid lockout. Remove old or unused numbers. Issue Resolution: If unable to update your number, clear browser cache and cookies, then retry. If verification code is not received, check your phone signal and verify your number is correct. For persistent issues, contact IT support for manual update. References: Update phone number for MFA Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support if you have trouble updating your phone number.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Use-FIDO2-Key..summary: Description Steps to use a FIDO2 security key to sign in to Microsoft 365 services. Details To use a FIDO2 security key to sign in: Go to the sign-in page for Microsoft 365 or Entra ID. Enter your username and select "Sign in with security key". Insert or tap your FIDO2 key when prompted. Enter your key PIN if required. Complete sign-in. Tips: Use a supported browser and device. Register backup keys for redundancy. Issue Resolution: If key is not recognized, try a different USB port or NFC reader and check for firmware updates. If PIN is not accepted, reset your key or contact IT. If unable to sign in, use an alternate method and contact IT for troubleshooting. References: Use FIDO2 key to sign in Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support if you have trouble using your FIDO2 key.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Use-TAP.html.title: How to Request and Use a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_Use-TAP.html.summary: Description Instructions for requesting and using a Temporary Access Pass for authentication. Details To request and use a Temporary Access Pass (TAP): Contact your IT administrator to request a TAP. Receive the TAP code securely. Go to the sign-in page for Microsoft 365 or Entra ID. Enter your username and select "Sign in with Temporary Access Pass". Enter the TAP code. Register new authentication methods if prompted. Complete sign-in and setup. Tips: TAP is time-limited; use it before it expires. Register backup methods during TAP sign-in. Issue Resolution: If TAP does not work, check for typos and ensure it has not expired. If unable to register new methods, try a different browser or device. If you do not receive a TAP, contact IT and confirm your identity. References: Temporary Access Pass Additional Information and Follow-up Contact IT support if you need a TAP or have trouble signing in.

docs/knowledgebase/KB_MFA_What-is-TAP.ht.summary: Description Overview of Temporary Access Pass (TAP) and its use cases for authentication. Details Temporary Access Pass (TAP) is a time-limited, single-use pass issued by IT for onboarding, recovery, or lost device scenarios. Use Cases: First-time setup of passwordless authentication. Recovery when all other authentication methods are unavailable. Device replacement or migration. How TAP Works: TAP is generated by an administrator and sent securely to the user. User enters TAP during sign-in to register new authentication methods. TAP expires after a set period or after use. Issue Resolution: If you do not receive a TAP, contact IT and confirm your identity. If TAP does not work, check for typos and ensure it has not expired. If unable to register new methods, try a different browser or device. References: Temporary Access Pass overview Additional Information and Follow-up Contact your IT support to request a TAP if needed.

docs/legacy/KB0010180_Active-Directory-R.title: Active Directory - Restore Deleted Objects from Recycle Bin | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/legacy/KB0010180_Active-Directory-R.summary: Description The Active Directory Recycle Bin feature, available since Windows Server 2008 R2, allows administrators to restore deleted Active Directory objects without performing an authoritative restore from backup. This feature addresses the critical need to recover accidentally deleted users, groups, computers, organizational units, and other AD objects, providing a time-limited recovery window that can prevent significant business disruption. The Recycle Bin maintains deleted objects in a special container where they retain their original attributes, Security Identifiers (SIDs), and group memberships, enabling complete restoration with full fidelity. This eliminates the complexity and time requirements of traditional authoritative restore procedures from system state backups. Use Cases: Recovery of accidentally deleted user accounts, preventing immediate access loss Restoration of security groups that could affect application permissions across multiple systems Recovery of computer objects that maintain domain trust relationships Restoration of organizational units and their contained objects as a complete hierarchy Quick recovery of service accounts critical to application functionality Details Prerequisites and Initial Setup Before using the Active Directory Recycle Bin, it must be enabled at the forest functional level. Critical Note: Once enabled, the Recycle Bin feature cannot be disabled and applies to the entire forest. Forest Functional Level Requirements: Minimum: Windows Server 2008 R2 Recommended: Current supported Windows Server version for optimal feature support To enable the Recycle Bin: # Enable for the entire forest (replace with your domain FQDN) Enable-ADOptionalFeature -Identity 'Recycle Bin Feature' -Scope ForestOrConfigurationSet -Target 'your-domain.com' # Verify enablement status Get-ADOptionalFeature -Filter 'name -like "Recycle Bin Feature"' Object Lifecycle and Recovery Phases The recovery window is controlled by the Deleted Object Lifetime (DOL), which defaults to 180 days but can be customized based on organizational requirements. Phase 1 - Logically Deleted (Recoverable): Objects move to the Deleted Objects container (cn=deleted objects,dc=domain,dc=com) isDeleted attribute set to True All original attributes preserved, including SID and group memberships Objects remain fully recoverable until DOL expires Duration: Default 180 days (configurable) Phase 2 - Tombstoned (Non-recoverable from Recycle Bin): isRecycled attribute becomes True after DOL expiration Most object attributes are stripped except essential identifiers Objects exist only to inform other domain controllers of deletion Cannot be restored using Recycle Bin methods Duration: Tombstone Lifetime (TSL), default 180 days Phase 3 - Physically Deleted: Objects permanently removed by Garbage Collection process Occurs after TSL expiration No recovery possible without authoritative restore from backup Recovery Operations Using PowerShell The following commands require the Active Directory PowerShell module and appropriate permissions (typically Domain Admins or delegated restore permissions). Essential Commands for Object Discovery # List all deleted objects with essential information Get-ADObject -Filter {isDeleted -eq $true} -IncludeDeletedObjects -Properties Name,LastKnownParent,ObjectClass,WhenChanged,WhenCreated | Format-Table Name, LastKnownParent, ObjectClass, WhenChanged -AutoSize # Search for specific deleted objects by name Get-ADObject -Filter {(isDeleted -eq $true) -and (name -like "*search-term*")} -IncludeDeletedObjects -Properties * # Find deleted objects by object class Get-ADObject -Filter {(isDeleted -eq $true) -and (objectClass -eq "user")} -IncludeDeletedObjects -Properties Name,LastKnownParent,WhenChanged Single Object Restoration # Restore object to its original location Get-ADObject -Filter {(isDeleted -eq $true) -and (name -eq "UserAccount")} -IncludeDeletedObjects | Restore-ADObject # Preview restoration without making changes Get-ADObject -Filter {(isDeleted -eq $true) -and (name -eq "UserAccount")} -IncludeDeletedObjects | Restore-ADObject -WhatIf Multiple Object Restoration # Restore multiple objects with similar names Get-ADObject -Filter {(isDeleted -eq $true) -and (name -like "*department*")} -IncludeDeletedObjects | Restore-ADObject # Restore all objects deleted within a specific timeframe $DateThreshold = (Get-Date).AddDays(-7) Get-ADObject -Filter {(isDeleted -eq $true) -and (whenChanged -ge $DateThreshold)} -IncludeDeletedObjects | Restore-ADObject Advanced Restoration Scenarios # Restore object to a different organizational unit Get-ADObject -Filter {(isDeleted -eq $true) -and (name -eq "UserAccount")} -IncludeDeletedObjects | Restore-ADObject -TargetPath "OU=RecoveredUsers,OU=Users,DC=domain,DC=com" # Restore with error handling and logging $DeletedObjects = Get-ADObject -Filter {(isDeleted -eq $true) -and (name -like "*project*")} -IncludeDeletedObjects foreach ($Object in $DeletedObjects) { try { Restore-ADObject -Identity $Object -ErrorAction Stop Write-Output "Successfully restored: $($Object.Name)" } catch { Write-Warning "Failed to restore $($Object.Name): $($_.Exception.Message)" } } Information Active Directory Administrative Center (ADAC) GUI Method For administrators who prefer graphical interfaces, ADAC provides an intuitive way to manage the Recycle Bin: Access ADAC: Run dsac.exe or launch from Server Manager Tools Navigate to Deleted Objects: Select your domain, then "Deleted Objects" container Filter and Search: Use built-in filters to locate specific deleted objects Restore Objects: Right-click desired objects and select "Restore" or "Restore To..." Troubleshooting Common Restoration Issues Error: "The operation could not be performed because the object's parent is either uninstantiated or deleted." Root Cause: The deleted object's parent container (OU) has also been deleted Resolution: Restore the parent container hierarchy before restoring child objects Prevention: Always check for dependent parent-child relationships before restoration Error: "An attempt was made to add an object to the directory with a name that is already in use." Root Cause: An object with the same distinguished name already exists (often recreated after deletion) Resolution Strategy 1: Use -TargetPath parameter to restore to a different OU Resolution Strategy 2: Rename the conflicting existing object first Resolution Strategy 3: Restore with a different name using ADAC GUI Error: "Access is denied" or insufficient permissions Root Cause: Insufficient permissions to perform restore operations Required Permissions: Domain Admins or explicitly delegated restore permissions Custom Delegation: Can delegate "Restore deleted objects" permission to specific users/groups Error: "The specified object cannot be found" when attempting restoration Root Cause: Object may have passed into tombstone phase (isRecycled = True) Verification: Check isRecycled attribute value Alternative: If tombstoned, requires authoritative restore from backup Permission Requirements and Security Considerations Required Permissions for Recycle Bin Operations: Read Permissions: On Deleted Objects container Restore Permissions: "Restore deleted objects" extended right Default Groups: Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins have full access Custom Delegation: Can be delegated to specific users or groups for controlled access Security Best Practices: Principle of Least Privilege: Delegate restore permissions only to necessary personnel Audit Trail: Enable auditing for object restoration events (Event ID 5137) Change Control: Implement approval processes for critical object restorations Documentation: Maintain logs of restoration activities for compliance Regular Review: Periodically review who has restore permissions Monitoring and Preventive Measures Proactive Deletion Detection: # Script to monitor recent deletions $LastCheckTime = (Get-Date).AddHours(-1) $RecentDeletions = Get-ADObject -Filter {(isDeleted -eq $true) -and (whenChanged -ge $LastCheckTime)} -IncludeDeletedObjects -Properties * if ($RecentDeletions) { # Send alert email or log to monitoring system $RecentDeletions | Format-Table Name, ObjectClass, LastKnownParent, WhenChanged } Event Log Monitoring: Event ID 5141: Object deletion events in Security log Event ID 5137: Object restoration events in Security log Recommended Tools: System Center Operations Manager, PowerShell monitoring scripts Configuration and Optimization Customizing Deleted Object Lifetime: # View current DOL setting (default 180 days) Get-ADObject -Identity "CN=Directory Service,CN=Windows NT,CN=Services,CN=Configuration,DC=domain,DC=com" -Properties msDS-DeletedObjectLifetime # Modify DOL (requires Enterprise Admin permissions) Set-ADObject -Identity "CN=Directory Service,CN=Windows NT,CN=Services,CN=Configuration,DC=domain,DC=com" -Replace @{'msDS-DeletedObjectLifetime'=365} Performance Considerations: Large numbers of deleted objects can impact LDAP query performance Consider regular cleanup of old deleted objects in high-deletion environments Monitor Deleted Objects container size in large environments Integration with Backup and Recovery Strategy Complementary Approaches: System State Backups: Essential for objects beyond tombstone lifetime Virtual Machine Snapshots: Quick recovery for test environments Third-party AD Recovery Tools: Enhanced features for complex scenarios Documentation: Maintain recovery procedures for various scenarios Recovery Time Objectives: Recycle Bin Recovery: Minutes to hours (depending on discovery time) Authoritative Restore: Hours to days (depending on backup location and size) Complete AD Rebuild: Days to weeks (worst-case scenario) Additional Information and Follow-up Alternative Recovery Methods When objects cannot be recovered through the Recycle Bin (due to exceeding tombstone lifetime or other limitations), consider these alternatives: Authoritative Restore from System State Backup: Requires recent system state backup containing the deleted objects More complex procedure involving directory service restore mode Can recover objects beyond tombstone lifetime May require coordination with other domain controllers Third-Party Active Directory Recovery Solutions: Commercial tools offering enhanced recovery capabilities Often provide more granular recovery options May include features like AD object comparison and selective attribute restoration Examples: Quest Recovery Manager, Semperis Active Directory Forest Recovery Compliance and Audit Considerations Regulatory Requirements: Document all object restoration activities for audit trails Maintain logs of who performed restorations and when Ensure restored objects meet compliance requirements (GDPR, SOX, HIPAA) Consider data retention policies when configuring DOL settings Change Management Integration: Incorporate restoration procedures into change management processes Require approval for restoration of critical security objects Maintain communication protocols for significant restorations Document business justification for object recovery Advanced Scenarios and Edge Cases Cross-Domain Object Dependencies: Objects with cross-domain group memberships may require additional verification Universal group memberships are preserved during restoration Domain-local group memberships in other domains may need manual verification Large-Scale Restoration Projects: Bulk restoration of OUs and their contents requires careful planning Consider restoration order (parents before children) Monitor replication impact during large restoration operations Plan for potential naming conflicts in bulk scenarios Service Account and Application Integration: Restored service accounts may need password resets Application configurations may need updates post-restoration Kerberos ticket caches may need clearing for restored computer accounts Certificate-based authentication may require certificate reissuance Integration with Modern Identity Solutions Hybrid Identity Considerations: Azure AD Connect synchronization impact of restored objects Office 365 license reassignment for restored user accounts Multi-factor authentication settings preservation Conditional access policy application to restored accounts PowerShell DSC and Automation: # Example DSC configuration snippet for automated monitoring Configuration ADRecycleBinMonitoring { Import-DscResource -ModuleName PSDesiredStateConfiguration Script MonitorDeletedObjects { GetScript = { $RecentDeletions = Get-ADObject -Filter {(isDeleted -eq $true) -and (whenChanged -ge ((Get-Date).AddDays(-1)))} -IncludeDeletedObjects return @{Result = $RecentDeletions.Count} } SetScript = { # Alert logic here } TestScript = { $RecentDeletions = Get-ADObject -Filter {(isDeleted -eq $true) -and (whenChanged -ge ((Get-Date).AddDays(-1)))} -IncludeDeletedObjects return ($RecentDeletions.Count -eq 0) } } } Related Technologies and Future Considerations Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) Integration: Cloud-only objects don't benefit from on-premises Recycle Bin Azure AD has its own deleted user recovery capabilities (30-day retention) Hybrid scenarios require coordination between on-premises and cloud recovery Windows Server Future Versions: Stay informed about enhancements to Recycle Bin functionality Consider migration paths to newer Windows Server versions Evaluate new features that may improve recovery capabilities Training and Knowledge Transfer Staff Training Requirements: Basic Operations: All IT staff should understand basic Recycle Bin concepts Advanced Recovery: Designated personnel trained in complex restoration scenarios Emergency Procedures: Clear escalation paths for critical object deletions Regular Drills: Practice recovery procedures in test environments Documentation Updates: Keep procedures current with environmental changes Cost-Benefit Analysis Recycle Bin Benefits: Reduced recovery time from hours/days to minutes Lower administrative overhead compared to authoritative restores Preserved object attributes and relationships Reduced reliance on backup systems for common scenarios Considerations: Storage overhead for deleted objects (minimal in most environments) Cannot be disabled once enabled Does not replace need for regular backups Requires proper planning and staff training References and Further Reading Enable the Active Directory Recycle Bin (Microsoft Learn) Get-ADObject PowerShell Documentation Restore-ADObject PowerShell Documentation Active Directory Recycle Bin Step-by-Step Guide (Microsoft Learn) Understanding Active Directory forest functional level and Recycle Bin status Planning: Develop comprehensive procedures for object restoration and documentation Testing: Practice restoration procedures in a test environment with various scenarios Implementation: Enable the Recycle Bin if not already active (irreversible decision) Training: Ensure IT staff are familiar with restoration procedures and best practices Monitoring: Implement proactive monitoring for object deletions and restoration activities Integration: Incorporate recovery procedures into change management and incident response processes Documentation: Create organization-specific procedures and maintain current operational documentation

docs/legacy/KB0011525_Email-How-to-submi.title: Email - How to submit Phish from the Outlook (Windows or Mac) or Web (OWA) client | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/legacy/KB0011525_Email-How-to-submi.summary: Description Messages that are marked as “junk” are automatically moved to your Junk Email folder. However, spammers and phishing attempts are continually evolving. Junk email received in your inbox can be reported to Microsoft by using the Report Message add-in. Reporting and sending a copy of the message to Microsoft will help them improve their spam filters. Email delivered to your Junk Email folder that is not spam can be marked as a legitimate message using the Report Message add-in as well. Details What is junk email? Junk email messages are typically referred to as spam. These are messages that you don't want to receive that may be advertising products you don't use or find offensive. If you choose the?"Junk"?option, a copy of the message may be?sent to Microsoft to help update their spam filters, and the message will be moved from your Inbox to your Junk Email folder.? What is phishing? Phishing is the practice of luring you into disclosing personal information, such as bank account numbers and passwords. Often phishing messages look legitimate but have deceptive links that actually open fake websites. If you select?"Phishing," a copy of your message may be sent to Microsoft to help update their filters, and the message will be moved from your Inbox to your Junk Email folder.? What is a legitimate email? If you know the sender and you're expecting the message, or if you receive a message that's mistakenly marked as junk, you can use the Report Message add-in to mark the message as?"Not Junk." This will move the message from the Junk Email folder back to your Inbox.? Information The following instructions will cover the reporting of suspected phishing emails using the “Report Message Add-In” in the Outlook desktop, web, and mobile clients. This will allow you to report the message as “Junk” or “Phishing” and send a copy of the email to Microsoft. Outlook Desktop (Windows or Mac) The Report Message button add-in will appear at the top of your Outlook client. To report an email as a phishing email: Open the message and click the Report Message button The Report Message Add-in will present you with several different options: Junk - Report the message as Spam Phishing - Report the message as a Phish Not Junk - Report an email incorrectly reported as Junk as a legitimate message Options - See options for the Report Message Add-in Help - Display Help Choosing Options from the Report Message button allows you to choose whether messages are automatically sent to Microsoft when they're reported as junk or phishing attempts. Change your Report Message options: Choose Options from the Report Message button on the Ribbon Select one of the following options: Always send a copy of the message to Microsoft Never send a copy of the message to Microsoft Ask before sending a copy of the message to Microsoft Once you've made your selection, choose Save. You'll see the following message in the InfoBar in the message header confirming your changes were saved successfully. Outlook Web (aka OWA) In the web client, there is not a Report Message button like there is in the Desktop client To report an email as a phishing email: Click the message and click the Junk button. Select either Junk or Phishing from the drop-down menu a. If you click Junk you will receive the following dialog box. b. Click Report (Optionally you can check the box to automatically report) c. If you click Junk you will receive the following dialog box. Click Report: Additional Information and Follow-up Contact the Help Desk at extension x6666 if you have any questions about the information listed above.

docs/legacy/KB0011532_How-to-Grant-Share.title: How to Grant Shared Calendar Permissions | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/legacy/KB0011532_How-to-Grant-Share.summary: Description Grant a user(s) permissions to a shared mailbox calendar. Details * Users who have full access permissions to shared mailboxes have the ability to grant permissions to other users who do not have access to the shared mailbox without submitting a ServiceNow ticket. * Full Access and Calendar permissions are two separate permissions. * Full Access Permissions: This permission provides a user(s) full access to everything about the mailbox. Granting this permission will require submitting a ticket to the Help Desk. * Calendar Permissions: This permission only provides a user(s) permission to the calendar which does not require submitting a ticket to the Help Desk. * These instructions ONLY provides a user(s) certain permissions to the calendar. This does not provide any other permissions like viewing the inbox or sending emails from the shared mailbox. * A user(s) needing permissions to a calendar does not necessarily need full access permissions to the shared mailbox. docs/legacy/KB0011582_Email-Spam-Notific.summary: Description Technology Services is constantly improving our security when it comes to email-based threats. Improvements to our policies have reduced the number of successful phishing attacks across the organization. However, these improvements have also increased the potential for legitimate emails to be prevented from being delivered. Details In order to mitigate the loss of legitimate emails that are inappropriately categorized as spam, we will be enabling a feature that will send a Spam Notification email to users who have messages that were quarantined instead of being delivered. Information The Spam Notification email contains the following information: ![](/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=8fccea361b57d2909446975b234bcb3f) The number of quarantined messages listed and the date of the last message in the list A link to the Quarantine Page where all of the messages sent to quarantine can be viewed A list of messages intended for your mailbox that were quarantined instead of being delivered and information about each message: Sender – The sender’s name and email address of the quarantined message Subject – The subject line text of the quarantined message Date – The date and time (in UTC) that the message was quarantined Actions – The actions that you are able to perform for that message ![](/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=03ccea361b57d2909446975b234bcb3e) The actions available to you for each message will depend on how the message was categorized by Microsoft: Action Description Available for Categories Release Releases the message from quarantine so that it will be delivered to the inbox Spam, Bulk, Phishing Request Release Sends a request to admins to release the message from quarantine High Confidence Spam, High Confidence Phishing Review Displays details about the message All If an action, such as Release, is not available, this is due to the Microsoft categorization. docs/legacy/KB0011584_Authentication-Tro.title: Authentication - Troubleshooting Sign-in Problems (Azure AD) | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/legacy/KB0011584_Authentication-Tro.summary: Description This article provides guidance for troubleshooting a sign-in (authentication) error associated with an application protected by Azure Active Directory (AD). The article explains the types of information that should be collected to properly identify and resolve an authentication error on one's own, or to convey in a Help Desk request if further assistance is required. Details Identifying the cause of an authentication error is important for applying the appropriate solution. Being prepared with as much potentially relevant information as possible when researching the problem - or submitting a Help Desk ticket - can simplify the process and minimize access-interruption and delays. Information Collecting Information: When you are experiencing or assisting with a sign-in error, collect the following information: Capture error message – Copy and paste (preferred method) or take a screen shot of the error message. Sign-in issues involving Azure AD will show an error code that starts with “AADSTS” NOTE: Error codes and messages are subject to change. For current information on AADSTS error descriptions, fixes, and some suggested workarounds, visit: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/reference-error-codes **_(See below for information on using Microsoft's "Flagged Sign-ins" functionality in order to isolate sign-in attempts and reproduce sign-in errors as needed to obtain a code.) 2. Username – The username used for the sign-in attempt (e.g., wwolfpack@madisoncollege.edu) 3. Time – The date and time the sign-in error occurred 4. Application or applications – The application(s) where the user's attempted sign-in resulted in the error. Also provide the URL if applicable. 5. Client Application – The client application used when the sign-in error occurred (e.g., Outlook 2019, MS Teams, Outlook Mobile, Chrome, Edge) 6. Device information – Information about the device can assist support staff in resolving your issue * Device platform/version (e.g., iPhone 11, Windows 10, etc.) * Whether the device is Madison College owned/supported or a personally owned device * The location and workstation (if a network computer/thin client) from which the sign-in was attempted * If the sign-in was attempted via a virtual network, lab, or desktop Additional Info – Any other information about the failed sign-in that may assist support-staff (e.g., was there an MFA prompt, did it work in the past, works from one device or another, are multiple users experiencing this issue) Reply to follow-up information requests – Prompt responses to support-staff requests for clarification or additional information will facilitate timely and effective resolutions. Flagging Sign-ins Microsoft has introduced a feature to simplify locating a specific sign-in attempt among the many that may be logged in a given timeframe. The flagged sign-in feature gives the user the ability to enable flagging after receiving an error message. Doing so logs flagged sign-ins for review, facilitating replication of errors for troubleshooting purposes. Once the feature is enabled, sign-in attempts made within the subsequent 20 (twenty) minutes will be flagged for review. Please note, however, that only sign-in events from the same user, on the same browser and client device or computer will be flagged. The flagging automatically turns off after 20 minutes. The procedure for utilizing the flagging feature is as follows: A sign-in attempt results in an error. User clicks View details in the error page. In Troubleshooting details, clickEnable Flagging. When flagging is enabled, the display text will read "Disable Flagging." User closes the browser window. User opens a new browser window (in the same browser application) and attempts the same sign-in that failed. User captures the error-code information from the reproduced sign-in. Additional Information and Follow Up If you are unable to resolve the issue on your own, please submit a Help Desk request with the information collected above. This will help us to quickly identify and resolve the sign-in problem.

This whitespace is optimized for performance, but it is not returned to the file system. Details Garbage Collection Increase the garbage collection logging level from 0 to 1 in order to determine how much whitespace exists in a database. This change in logging level will result in an Event ID 1646 being logged to the Directory Service log. The event will show how much total space is used by the database file and how much recoverable whitespace exists. Open an elevated PowerShell prompt Stop the AD DS Service by typing: ? Stop-Service ntds -force Begin Compacting: Enter the command "ntdsutil" At the ntdsutil prompt, type "activate instance ntds" and press "ENTER" Type "files" and press "ENTER" To begin compacting the database type compact to "d:\NTDS\compact " If compacting completed with errors perform an integrity check (See Perform Integrity Check bellow) Finish Compacting: Rename "D:\NTDS

docs/legacy/KB0011588_Authentication-Acc.summary: Description This document describes controls that have been put in place to restrict remote access to college resources from some countries outside the US. Details The requirements for accessing college resources from outside the US are the same as those for accessing them from off-campus locations within the US. However, there is a list of countries, referred to as "Threat Countries," which, due to their high level of cyber-threat activity, are restricted by policy from accessing most college services. A student attempting to access college resources from a Threat Country will receive an error message similar to the one below. ![](/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=2ffcaa361b57d2909446975b234bcbc6) Information Campus Solutions remains accessible from these countries, but all other resources require the use of the Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) service. Students outside the US but not in a Threat Country need only to complete multifactor authentication to access college services directly on a personal mobile device or computer. Exemptions Students located in a Threat Country can be exempted from this policy by submitting their Name/Student ID to the Student Help Desk. docs/legacy/KB0011592_Active-Directory-C.title: Active Directory – Connect to Another Forest with PowerShell | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/legacy/KB0011592_Active-Directory-C.summary: Description Connect to an Active Directory Forest other than the one that the client host is a member of. Details PowerShell will automatically create a PSDrive for the Active Directory domain that the client is a member of. An additional PSDrive can be created for a different domain in another forest. Information The following command will create a PSDrive for a different domain than the one the host is joined to. New-PSDrive -Name <PSDrive-Name> -PSProvider ActiveDirectory -Server "<Domain-Controller>" -Scope Global c-credential (Get-Credential "<User-Name>") -root "//RootDSE/" The "-Scope Global" switch is required if you run this cmd-let from a script. The new PSDrive can be used in several ways. For example, to connect to the adtest.madisoncollege.edu forest with PowerShell from a host joined to the production ad.madisoncollege.edu forest. The following command will create a PSDrive named "ADTEST" that will be connected to the "adtest.wisc.edu" domain. New-PSDrive -Name ADTEST -PSProvider ActiveDirectory -Server "adtest.madisoncollege.edu" -Scope Global -credential (Get-Credential "ADTEST\<username>") -root "//RootDSE/" To use this PSDrive you can "cd" to the "ADTEST" PSDrive and then run the Active Directory modules as normal: cd ADTEST: Get-ADDomain The second method is to provide the "server" switch with the name of the domain controller: PS C:\> Get-ADDomain -server "adtest.madisoncollege.edu" The following code will check to see if the drive exists prior to attempting creation of the new PSDrive if (-not(Get-PSDrive TEST)) { New-PSDrive -Name ADTEST -PSProvider ActiveDirectory -Server "adtest.madisoncollege.edu" -Scope Global -credential (Get-Credential "ADTEST\<username>") -root "//RootDSE/" } Else { "Drive already exists" } Additional Information and Follow Up References: Active Directory Powershell: The Drive is the connection (Active Directory Powershell Blog) Using the New-PSDrive Cmdlet (TechNet) Using the Get-PSDrive Cmdlet (TechNet) Contact the the Identity and Access Management Team if you have any questions about the information listed above.

docs/legacy/KB0011633_Active-Directory-E.title: Active Directory - Enable Diagnostic Logging | Madison College Knowledge Base
docs/legacy/KB0011633_Active-Directory-E.summary: Description This article provides comprehensive guidance on enabling and configuring diagnostic logging for Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) and related components. Diagnostic logging is essential for troubleshooting domain controller issues, monitoring replication, and analyzing authentication problems in Active Directory environments. Proper diagnostic logging configuration enables administrators to capture detailed information about Active Directory operations, helping to identify and resolve issues related to authentication, replication, LDAP operations, and other critical domain services. Understanding how to enable, configure, and manage these logs is crucial for maintaining a healthy Active Directory infrastructure. Use Cases: Troubleshooting domain controller replication issues Diagnosing authentication and authorization problems Monitoring LDAP query performance and errors Investigating security-related events in Active Directory Analyzing network connectivity and communication issues between domain controllers Details Active Directory Diagnostic Logging Registry Location Diagnostic logging for domain controllers is centrally managed through the Windows Registry at: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NTDS\Diagnostics Each diagnostic category is controlled by a specific REG_DWORD entry that determines the verbosity level of logging for that particular service or component. Diagnostic Logging Categories The following table lists all available diagnostic logging categories and their corresponding registry entry IDs: Entry ID Service Description 1 Knowledge Consistency Checker (KCC) Monitors replication topology generation and maintenance 2 Security Events Tracks security-related operations and authentication events 3 ExDS Interface Events Logs Exchange Directory Service interface operations 4 MAPI Interface Events Records Messaging Application Programming Interface activities 5 Replication Events Monitors domain controller replication activities 6 Garbage Collection Tracks cleanup operations for deleted objects 7 Internal Configuration Records internal configuration changes and operations 8 Directory Access Logs directory access and query operations 9 Internal Processing Monitors internal AD DS processing activities 10 Performance Counters Records performance-related metrics and counters 11 Initialization/Termination Tracks service startup and shutdown events 12 Service Control Logs service control operations and management activities 13 Name Resolution Monitors DNS and NetBIOS name resolution activities 14 Backup Records backup and restore operations 15 Field Engineering Advanced debugging information for Microsoft support 16 LDAP Interface Events Logs LDAP protocol operations and queries 17 Setup Records installation and configuration activities 18 Global Catalog Monitors Global Catalog operations and queries 19 Inter-site Messaging Tracks communication between Active Directory sites 20 Group Caching Logs universal group membership caching activities 21 Linked-Value Replication Monitors linked attribute replication (group memberships) 22 DS RPC Client Records outbound RPC operations from domain controller 23 DS RPC Server Logs inbound RPC operations to domain controller 24 DS Schema Tracks schema-related operations and modifications Diagnostic Logging Levels Each diagnostic category can be configured with different verbosity levels, ranging from minimal logging to extensive debugging information: Value Level Description Performance Impact Recommended Use 0 None Only critical events and error events are logged Minimal Default production setting 1 Minimal Very high-level events and major task completions Low Initial troubleshooting when problem location is unknown 2 Basic Moderate level of detail with operational information Low General monitoring and basic troubleshooting 3 Extensive Detailed information including task steps and processes Medium Targeted troubleshooting when problem area is identified 4 Verbose Comprehensive logging with detailed operational data High Advanced troubleshooting requiring detailed analysis 5 Internal Complete logging including debug strings and all configuration changes Very High Deep troubleshooting for specific categories only Performance and Storage Considerations Important Warnings: Levels 4-5: Should only be used temporarily and for specific troubleshooting scenarios Production Impact: High verbosity logging can significantly impact domain controller performance Storage Requirements: Extensive logging can generate large volumes of log data rapidly Monitoring: Always monitor disk space when enabling verbose logging Best Practices: Enable verbose logging only for specific categories related to the problem Set logging back to level 0 or 1 after troubleshooting is complete Monitor Event Log sizes to prevent disk space issues Consider log rotation and archival strategies for extended troubleshooting periods Information View Current Logging Levels with PowerShell $Reg = "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NTDS\Diagnostics" Get-ItemProperty -Path $Reg Configure with PowerShell Use the following PowerShell example to configure logging levels: $Reg = "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NTDS\Diagnostics" Set-ItemProperty -Path $Reg -Name <service> -Type DWORD -Value <value> Example: Enable verbose replication logging: $Reg = "HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NTDS\Diagnostics" Set-ItemProperty -Path $Reg -Name "5 Replication Events" -Type DWORD -Value 3 Netlogon Logging Configuration After enabling Netlogon logging the activity will be logged to %windir%\debug\netlogon.log. Depending on the amount of activity you may want to increase the size of this log from the default 20 MB. When the file reaches 20 MB, it is renamed to Netlogon.bak, and a new Netlogon.log file is created. The size of the Netlogon.log file can be increased by changing the MaximumLogFileSize registry entry. This registry entry does not exist by default.
